solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Song, where it's found, and how one's done?

parts.note: a track is a song on an album
a song is found on a record, the vinyl disc

explanation.surface: A riddle about a song, the disc carrying it, and how someone has performed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two phrases build the answer piece by piece; the last phrase is the definition, a person's history of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A track record is the past performance by which someone is judged, so it tells how one has done.

clue.text: Twitch, regularly observed?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word Twitch, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A twitch that keeps recurring and gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of Twitch give the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: a twitch seen again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary, habitual muscle spasm, a twitch that recurs.

clue.text: A place for judge not left in chambers

indicators.note: not means the letter for left is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: a trial is where a judge presides

explanation.surface: Judges' chambers are a place for a judge, minus any left-wing leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like a judge's private rooms, which fits the surface, but here it means chambers of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are the two upper cavities of the heart, so they are its chambers.

clue.text: Warning: sharp cut will lead to rueful expression

indicators.note: will lead to means the first piece comes before the next
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: keen means sharp, as of a blade
a pout is a sulky or rueful face

explanation.surface: A warning that a sharp cut will make someone wince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks KEEN to KEE, which then leads POUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep out is a notice on a sign forbidding entry, a warning to stay away.

clue.text: Attention given to item about large life-form in solar System

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: about means the word for item goes around the letter for large

parts.note: a thing is an item
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone attending to a large organism somewhere in our solar system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is a creature of Earth, the life-bearing planet of our solar system, as science fiction calls humans.

clue.text: Leader ousted from fringe organisation.

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is removed from the word for fringe

parts.note: a border is a fringe or edge

explanation.surface: A fringe group whose leader has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fringe organisation, but 'fringe' is the word to cut and 'organisation' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means organisation, as in putting things in order, or a religious body.

clue.text: Scorn island lawyer in Manhattan getting involved in racket

indicators.note: getting involved in means the pieces go inside the word for racket

parts.note: din is a racket, a loud noise
IS is the map abbreviation for island
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A scornful island lawyer caught up in a New York racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests organised crime, but it is noise here.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt, the feeling of scorn for something unworthy.

clue.text: Job cut reversed in concession

indicators.note: reversed means the shortened word is read backwards
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a post is a job

explanation.surface: A job cut that is undone as a concession to workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks POST to POS, and 'reversed' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small appeasing gift or concession made to pacify someone.

clue.text: Figure poor-quality stuff is involved in a lot of criticism

indicators.note: involved in means these letters go inside the shortened word for criticism
a lot of means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in getting stick
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: A figure showing how much criticism concerns cheap rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick in the sense of criticism is informal British, as in 'taking stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a numerical datum, a figure in a set of data.

clue.text: No gin served up? One whisky short? He may be devastated!

indicators.note: served up means the words for no and gin read upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: nay means no
a gin is a snare, a trap for animals
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: malt is a type of whisky
the final letter of malt, removed because the whisky is short

explanation.surface: A drinker denied gin and a whisky short of what he wanted is distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: The questions sound like a reveller's complaints, but gin is a snare, not the drink. 'devastated' plays on its slang sense of very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A party animal is a dedicated reveller, the sort likely to end up wrecked, slang for very drunk, by the night's end.

clue.text: Complained about most of weight system providing security for climbers?

indicators.note: about means the word for complained goes around the other piece

parts.note: carped means complained

indicators.note: most of means dropping the last letter

parts.note: troy is a system of weights used for precious metals

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about weights while supplying safety kit to mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers; they are people going up stairs, held safe by the rods that keep a stair carpet in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet rod holds a stair carpet firmly against each step, keeping those who climb the stairs safe.

clue.text: What contributes to flight ace being held in prison

indicators.note: being held in means the letter goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: An ace pilot imprisoned, contributing to an escape flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' and 'ace' suggest aviation or escape; a flight here is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step, and many steps together make a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Scottish bay: surprised cry there after appearance of marine creature

indicators.note: after appearance of means the cry comes after the creature

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal
och is a Scottish exclamation, there referring back to Scotland

explanation.surface: At a Scottish bay, someone cries out when a seal pops up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Scotland, so the cry is the Scots och.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea loch is an arm of the sea reaching inland in Scotland, a coastal inlet.

clue.text: Recorder of earth movement that's wrecked gophers' aims

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters of the words before it are destroyed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An instrument tracking ground tremors has ruined the burrowing gophers' plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismograph is the instrument that records earthquakes and other ground tremors.

clue.text: Actual state of affairs regarding landed gentry, ultimately

parts.note: re means regarding or about
alit means landed, past tense of alight

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of gentry

explanation.surface: The real situation of the landed gentry, when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landed gentry' reads as one phrase, but landed is ALIT, as a bird alights.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is the true condition of things, how matters actually stand.

clue.text: I make a mark in logo

parts.note: to dent is to make a mark in a surface

explanation.surface: A graphic artist boasting about leaving their mark on a company logo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is a short broadcast identifier, such as a channel's logo sequence.

clue.text: Financial situation? Funny figures about operating after franchise's closure

indicators.note: after means the rest follows that final letter
closure means the final letter of the word franchise

parts.note: the word franchise, without its possessive ending

indicators.note: about means the word for funny figures goes around the word for operating

parts.note: comics are comedians, funny people
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Money trouble as a franchise closes, its comedians' fees in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny figures' suggests dodgy accounts, but they are comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics can mean the financial aspects of an undertaking, as in the economics of a deal.

clue.text: London district where no one returns around cocktail time

indicators.note: around means the reversed letters go around the cocktail and time
returns means the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sling is a gin-based cocktail, as in Singapore sling

explanation.surface: A London area where nobody goes home when it is cocktail hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one returns' reads as nobody going home, but the two words are reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough in north London.

clue.text: Initially lit the cigar awkwardly without much spark

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of lit
awkwardly means the letters of the cigar are jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily lighting a cigar that barely catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without much spark' fits the cigar's feeble glow, but it describes a sluggish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, with little spark or vigour.

clue.text: Beethoven sonata? Perform other work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the popular name of Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14
second meaning: to have a second job on the side

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pianist taking on extra pieces; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moonlight Sonata is a famous piano work, and moonlighting means taking a secondary job, often secretly.

clue.text: Fielder for one second blocking rising ball

indicators.note: blocking means these letters sit inside the reversed word, stopping it
rising means the word for ball reads upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a pill is a ball, as in old slang for a cricket or tennis ball
eg means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder who, for a moment, stops a ball that has bounced up.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg slip is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side; pill is old slang for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg slip is both a fielding position and the player standing there, so a fielder.

clue.text: Stand-in minister starts to organise choir in Mass? Not all of it

indicators.note: in means those first letters go inside the shortened word for mass
not all of it means dropping the last letter

parts.note: a lump is a mass

indicators.note: starts to means taking the first letters of organise and choir

explanation.surface: A substitute clergyman sets about arranging the choir for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital looks like the church service but is a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is someone covering temporarily for a doctor or clergyman, a substitute.

clue.text: I will avoid idiots after half-hearted expressions of sorrow

indicators.note: after means the idiots come after the word for half-hearted

parts.note: lame means feeble or half-hearted, as a lame excuse

indicators.note: will avoid means the letter I is left out of the word for idiots

parts.note: nits are idiots, nitwits

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to steer clear of fools after half-hearted apologies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' hints at removing a middle letter, but it is LAME; I leaves NITS to give NTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laments are cries or songs of grief, ways of voicing sorrow.

clue.text: Hanoverian monarch — not English — leading a Eurasian country

indicators.note: leading means the monarch's name comes before a
not means the letter for English is removed

parts.note: George I was the first Hanoverian king of Britain

explanation.surface: A German-born king, not English, at the head of a country straddling Europe and Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is GEORGE I, and dropping an E leaves GEORGI.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a nation in the Caucasus on the border between Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Cause concern? The French invading might

indicators.note: invading means the French article goes inside the word for might

parts.note: arm means might or power, as the arm of the law
la is French for the

explanation.surface: French forces invading would be cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun, power.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm is to frighten or worry someone, causing them concern.

clue.text: Top figure in the main almost entirely behind attitude about historic currency

indicators.note: behind means the last piece comes after the rest
about means the word for attitude goes around the currency

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude
DM is the Deutschmark, Germany's former currency

indicators.note: almost means dropping the final letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A leading figure's attitude to an old currency, almost entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea, so the top figure is a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking naval officer, the main being poetic for the open sea.

clue.text: Greek character providing home for popular endangered species?

indicators.note: providing home for means the Greek letter holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: rho is the 17th letter of the Greek alphabet
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A Greek person sheltering a well-loved animal at risk of extinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinos are large horned mammals, several kinds of which are critically threatened by poaching.

clue.text: Live portrayal finally capturing one Shakespeare character

indicators.note: capturing means those letters enclose the numeral for one

parts.note: are is a form of to be, to live or exist
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of portrayal

explanation.surface: A live stage portrayal at last captures one of Shakespeare's characters.
explanation.walkthrough: ARE and L capture I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in The Tempest.

clue.text: Skill acquiring information in a South American country

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for skill takes the information inside it

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone picking up skills and knowledge while in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a large nation in the south of South America, its capital Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Friend, heading off, had a meal

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend left early after eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate is the past tense of eat, so it means consumed food, had a meal.

clue.text: Husband is word appropriate to males

explanation.surface: A husband's word is suited to men.
explanation.definitionFit: His is the masculine possessive pronoun, used only of males.

clue.text: Lava turned up? Notices me after eruption

indicators.note: turned means the word up is read the other way round
after eruption means the letters of notices me burst out in a new order

explanation.surface: Lava has surfaced and seems to demand attention after a volcano blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrived, but up is reversed to PU; then the letters of NOTICES ME are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice stone is a light, porous rock formed from frothy lava cooling rapidly.
